_doc: PUBLICATION-1 (owner, 2026-11-15): every repository of the org is public under USL-1.0 (free for non-commercial use, commercial licence for commercial use, share-alike, no patents asserted, defensive disclosure), and publishing is a procedure the code runs, not a decision anyone re-makes. Read by foundation/publication.py: `python3 -m foundation publication --check|--audit|--plan|--flip`. `--check` is part of the doctrine step. A flip is refused until the audit is clean over full history; a history that cannot be read in full (shallow clone) is `unmeasured`, never clean. The procedure and lessons below are data the check enforces; changed only by a reviewed PR.

procedure.does: for EVERY repo in `repos`, on a full mirror (all branches, tags, pull refs): scan every commit for secret patterns; a hit is cleared only by an exact history_allow entry (path + sha256 + reason); shallow or unreadable is unmeasured
per repo, list tripwire paths at HEAD; each needs a disposition (publish, move, remove) in ops/publication/reviewed.json, keyed `<repo>:<path>` (bare path for this repo)
scan issue, pull request and comment text of every repo (text_surfaces) with the same patterns
read live visibility; a repo that is already public must have secret scanning and push protection on
required files present in EVERY repo, SPDX id present, licence text identical across repos (license/scripts/check-copies.mjs)

per repo in flip_order, only on that repo's own clean audit: gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences, then verify unauthenticated and turn on secret scanning and push protection
procedure.gate: IC-GATE-001 residue: needs an org-admin token; default in effect is stay private until the audit is clean

routes: tick Worker with the GitHub App consent screen (POINT-AND-CLICK-1)
credential.default_in_effect: repositories stay as they are; no step fails open

lessons.lesson: A cloud code session's GitHub tools cannot change repository visibility and gh is barred there; the flip is owned by a server-side route holding ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN, never by a session.
Session clones are shallow; a secret scan of them proves nothing about history. Shallow means unmeasured.
Publishing exposes full history and forks and caches cannot be undone; the flip refuses until the audit is clean.
The licence text is immutable and a protected path; publication never edits it, and the copies must stay identical.
A refused action is recorded and the next route taken; it is never re-worded past the same check.
The audit read only the repo it ran in while the flip covered seven. Each repo is flipped only on its own full-mirror audit; one repo never vouches for another.
Issues, pull request bodies and comments become public with the repo and are scanned like history.
ops and seed had no licence files and spec no top-level LICENSE while this repo passed; required files are checked in every repo.
A placeholder token in history cannot be removed without a rewrite. It is cleared only by an exact entry (path, sha256 of the match, reason), never by loosening a pattern or allowing a folder.

ultrastable/ultrastable was public from creation with secret scanning off while the record said private. Visibility and scanning state are read from the API, never assumed; a public repo without push protection is not clean.
ip/ (127 files) was not a tripwire although the standing rule is never to publish ip, business, funding or investor material without a recorded disposition.
The procedure said verify unauthenticated and the code did not. A flip is done only when the repo answers an unauthenticated request and protection is on.
The hand-off prompt for this work was saved in a cloud session scratchpad and was gone when the next session looked. What a later session must run lives in the repo.
Actions run logs also become public and are not scanned yet. A surface nobody measures is listed as unmeasured in the policy and the ledger, with an open loop, never left out.
Five clean repos were held by tripwires in a repo that was already public. Refusal is per repo with its reasons in the ledger.

history_allow.reason: test input to the redaction guard: the header line only, no key body
placeholder token (alphabet then digits) in the review gate self-test string
same match, as seen by the in-repo audit of this repo
